epistemic_contract: These are open research questions, not repository claims. Status must be revised when new observations or theory change the evidence.

questions.question: What is the microscopic identity of dark matter?
questions.importance: Gravity constrains abundance and distribution but not uniquely the particle, field, compact-object or multi-component content.
equations: dR/dE_R = (rho_chi/m_chi) N_T integral f(v) v d sigma/dE_R d^3v
questions.current_evidence: Multiple gravitational probes support an additional non-baryonic component in the standard cosmological framework; no universally accepted microscopic detection exists.
competing_hypotheses: primordial black holes in allowed windows
questions.decisive_measurement: A reproducible non-gravitational signal with independently verified mass/coupling properties that also remains consistent with astrophysical abundance and structure.
questions.falsification: Candidate-specific parameter regions can be excluded; no single null result falsifies all dark matter.

questions.question: What sets the inner structure of dark-matter haloes?
questions.importance: Cores, cusps and substructure connect microphysics to baryonic feedback and numerical modelling.
questions.current_evidence: Resolved galaxies show diverse inner rotation-curve shapes; baryonic feedback and halo response are important systematics.
questions.decisive_measurement: A cross-scale signature that follows one microphysical interaction law after baryonic and selection effects are controlled.
questions.falsification: A proposed microphysics model fails if it cannot reproduce jointly galaxies, substructure and cluster constraints.

questions.question: What is the local Milky Way dark-matter phase-space distribution?
questions.importance: Direct-detection rates and directional signatures depend on density and velocity structure near the Solar neighbourhood.
questions.current_evidence: Stellar dynamics constrain local density and kinematics but depend on tracer, equilibrium and Galactic-potential assumptions.
questions.decisive_measurement: Consistent dynamical reconstruction plus a directional non-gravitational signal mapping the same phase-space features.
questions.falsification: Specific smooth-halo models can be rejected by incompatible directional or dynamical structure.

questions.question: Does dark matter self-interact?
questions.importance: Self-interactions can alter halo cores, shapes and merging-cluster dynamics.
questions.current_evidence: Cluster and galaxy constraints are velocity- and model-dependent; no unique nonzero self-interaction has been established.
questions.decisive_measurement: A repeatable velocity-dependent scattering signature across independently modelled systems.
questions.falsification: A proposed cross-section law is ruled out if it simultaneously conflicts with cluster and galaxy-scale structure.

questions.question: Is dark matter one component or an extended dark sector?
questions.importance: Multiple states and mediators change production, structure, detection and possible technology.
questions.current_evidence: Current gravitational data do not require a single microscopic species.
questions.decisive_measurement: Two or more correlated dark-sector observables that cannot be fit by one effective component.
questions.falsification: Specific sector models fail joint cosmological, laboratory and structure constraints.

questions.question: Are extra dimensions relevant to dark-sector physics?
questions.importance: Extra-dimensional models can generate Kaluza-Klein states or new mediators, but electromagnetic darkness alone does not require them.
questions.current_evidence: No extra spatial dimension is established as the explanation for dark matter.
questions.decisive_measurement: A model-specific spectrum or force-law deviation independently reproduced and consistent with a dark-matter abundance mechanism.
questions.falsification: Non-observation excludes model-specific compactification/coupling regions, not the entire idea at once.

questions.question: How completely can baryonic physics mimic small-scale dark-matter signatures?
questions.importance: Feedback, gas flows and stellar populations can reshape the same observables used to infer halo microphysics.
questions.current_evidence: Baryons matter strongly in galaxy centres, but the degree of degeneracy varies by system and scale.
questions.decisive_measurement: Joint baryonic-history and gravitational constraints across systems selected independently of the anomaly.
questions.falsification: A proposed feedback mechanism fails if its required energy/history is inconsistent with observed stellar populations.

questions.question: Which observations most cleanly distinguish dark matter from modified-gravity explanations?
questions.importance: Galaxy regularities alone can be degenerate with phenomenological acceleration laws.
equations: relativistic lensing field equations for the tested theory
questions.current_evidence: The standard dark-matter framework fits multiple independent cosmological and lensing probes; alternative frameworks require complete relativistic predictions to be compared fairly.
questions.decisive_measurement: A pre-registered cross-scale prediction on which complete theories differ and systematics are controlled.
questions.falsification: Theory-specific predictions fail if they cannot jointly fit the discriminating data.

questions.question: What properties would have to be discovered before dark matter could become an engineering medium?
questions.importance: Discovery does not imply capture, energy extraction, communication or propulsion.
equations: rest-energy ceiling/A = eta rho v c^2
questions.current_evidence: Known searches target extraordinarily weak interactions; no demonstrated capture, confinement or controllable conversion mechanism exists.
questions.decisive_measurement: A reproducible controllable interaction followed by demonstrated capture/confinement and quantified energy or momentum transfer.
questions.falsification: If surviving dark matter couples only gravitationally at inaccessible strengths, most material-engineering scenarios fail.
